rows.explanation: A large number of residents in our district do not have college degrees, and many also face language barriers. Investing in targeted vocational training, along with NYOD English language classes, is a priority that could help raise the low incomes many families are currently experiencing. Our residents are intelligent and capable, and they would benefit from training focused on high-paying, in-demand skills, as well as improving their English proficiency. Currently, there are no Work Force 1 (WF1) centers nearby to serve our district, so providing funding to fill this gap would be a valuable investment. We are requesting that Work Force 1 collaborate with our local CBO, the Boro Park Jewish Community Council, and our local public libraries to provide these vital services to our community.

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: We have a large number of small commercial corridors in our district (i.e.; Avenue U, Sheepshead Bay Road, Avenue P, Gravesend Neck Road and Avenue X) with rents sky-rocketing to ludicrous heights. These storefronts either turnover rapidly, or sit vacant warehoused without attracting new businesses or new investment in the community. Empty storefronts don't entice consumers. They reduce foot traffic to the corridors. Things have gone from bad to worse. The City needs to offer indepedent small business owners more incentives and assistance in creating businesses, or offer property owners some incentives to attract and retain businesses. Outrageous rents are keeping many of our small commercial areas bleak and depressed.
rows.headline: Other commercial district revitalization requests
rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports and can accommodate Explanation: SBS has made investments in commercial corridors in the district through a variety of grants. SBS has supported local commercial revitalization through the Kings Highway BID, which received Small BID Grants this Fiscal Year and in FY24 and a Commercial District Lighting grant in FY24. This Fiscal Year, SBS also provided the Brooklyn Alliance, who previously deployed select interventions along the commercial corridors in the district through an Avenue NYC grant SBS provided, a Merchant Organizing grant to support commercial districts and merchant organizing in the community. SBS will continue to promote grant programs when available and encourage the community boards to share information about our grant programs with local non-profits. While commercial rents are set by private commercial property-owners and the city does not have an ability to regulate commercial rents, SBS is proud to deliver up to 40 hours of pro-bono Commercial Lease Assistance Program. This service provides businesses legal representation as they negotiate commercial leases and rents with landlords either at the point of signing a new lease, renewing a lease, or supporting pre-litigation issues.

rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports and can accommodate Explanation: SBS provides, both virtually and in-person at our Business Solutions Centers, businesses 1-1 support, courses and webinars, support in accessing capital, and free legal services. Through our business education offering, we offer free business courses/webinars to help businesses with digital marketing. Please call the SBS Hotline for more information and to receive a referral to services at (888) SBS-4NYC. Two years ago, SBS also launched "NYC Funds Finder", a platform for business owners seeking capital which they can visit at nycfundsfinder.nextstreet.com. Additionally, SBS offers the NYC Future Fund, a revenue-based loan that addressing the gap in access to affordable capital faced by small business owners, particularly those that otherwise often cannot obtain traditional bank financing Finally, SBS offers commercial revitalization grants to community-based organizations that can include support with marketing. SBS will continue emailing community boards when grants are available and open for applications, and we encourage community boards to blast it to their networks.
